# Jāgariya Sutta (Iti 47 (It 2.20 PTS It 41))

**ID:** Iti 47 (It 2.20 PTS It 41)  
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Jāgariya Sutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jāgariya Sutta* ("Wake Up", Iti 47; PTS It 41) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The text instructs practitioners to abide wakeful, mindful, alert, centered, sensitive, clear, and calm, and at the proper time to see clearly into skillful mental qualities. T. W. Rhys Davids references this discourse as an illustration of the arahant being described as *sambodhi-parāyana* ("intent on full awakening") [Rhys Davids, Dialogues of the Buddha].

A full parallel to the discourse is preserved in the Chinese canon as T 765.82 (覺悟). In addition, passage-level parallels are found in the *Smṛtivarga* of various *Udānavarga* recensions (Sanskrit UV 15, UVS 15; Tibetan Uv Kg 15) and Chinese verse collections (T 210.6, T 212.16, and T 213.15).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: T 765.82 覺悟
- Passage-level parallels: UV 15 Smṛtivarga; T 210.6 惟念品法句經第六十有二章; T 212.16 惟念品第十六; T 213.15 法集要頌經憶念品第十五; Uv Kg 15 Reflection; UVS 15 Smṛtivarga

**Sources**

- [Rhys Davids, Dialogues of the Buddha] T. W. Rhys Davids, Dialogues of the Buddha (1899) — Citation of Iti 47 in connection with the term sambodhi-parāyana describing the arahant.
